facts.text: panda-gym is a set of robotic environments based on the PyBullet physics engine and gymnasium
The documented use is gym.make('PandaReach-v3', render_mode='human') followed by reset() and step(action)
PandaReach-v3 is registered with entry point panda_gym.envs:PandaReachEnv, kwargs reward_type='sparse' and control_type='ee', and max_episode_steps=50 (100 only for Stack)
PandaReachEnv builds the Panda robot with block_gripper=True, so the gripper is not part of the action
Panda's action space is Box(-1.0, 1.0, shape=(n_action,)) in float32, with n_action 3 for end-effector control and 7 for joint control, plus one for the gripper when it is not blocked
An end-effector action moves the target by at most 0.05 per step and the target height is clipped to 0 or above
The Reach distance_threshold defaults to 0.05 and goal_range to 0.3
The Reach goal is drawn uniformly from goal_range_low [-0.15, -0.15, 0] to goal_range_high [0.15, 0.15, 0.3]
distance is the Euclidean norm rounded to 6 decimals
Reach.is_success returns True when the distance is below the threshold
The sparse Reach reward is -1 outside the threshold and 0 inside it; the dense reward is minus the distance
Panda.get_obs returns the end-effector position and velocity, and omits the finger width when the gripper is blocked
Reach has no task-specific observation and its achieved goal is the end-effector position
RobotTaskEnv concatenates the robot and task observations and adds the achieved and desired goals
The RobotTaskEnv observation space is a Dict of three Box(-10.0, 10.0) members
RobotTaskEnv.reset seeds gym.Env, gives the task the same generator, resets the robot and the task, and returns is_success
Panda.reset sets the neutral joint values
Reach.reset samples a new goal and places the target there
RobotTaskEnv.step applies the action, advances the simulation once, terminates on task success, sets truncated=False and computes the reward
PyBullet sets the physics timestep to 1/500 s and exposes dt as timestep * n_substeps
n_substeps defaults to 20
PyBullet.step advances n_substeps physics steps per call
The runtime dependencies are gymnasium>=0.26, pybullet, numpy<2 and scipy

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reseeds gym.Env and the task shares that generator (core.py:276-286), so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake samples goals with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so one seed gives different goals on the two

gaps: rigid-body PyBullet model of a Franka Panda arm, a table and a target sphere; the fake moves the end-effector by the clipped action times 0.05 and models neither inverse kinematics nor contacts, friction, actuators or sensor noise
no rendering: render_mode is not served and the fake has no renderer
the fake samples goals with Python's random.Random while upstream draws them from numpy's generator, so one seed can give different goals and trajectories
the fake applies the 50-step TimeLimit that gymnasium.make adds to PandaReach-v3; RobotTaskEnv.step itself never truncates
no snapshot and restore through get_state/set_state; the upstream environment has save_state, restore_state and remove_state, which the bridge does not use
the fake's start end-effector position is test data, not a calibrated model, so its trajectories were not compared with a PyBullet run
observations are Python float lists; upstream returns float32 numpy arrays of the same six (robot) and three (goal) values

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
